coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K04. CNSS requires employer registration within 8 days and worker registration within 8 days of hire; no Togolese text found on domestic workers specifically. An IOM report mentions a Togolese agency placing home-care staff.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Export ban on scrap since interministerial order 014/MCICL/MEF/MPI of 7 Apr 2021, replaced by a 2 Feb 2024 Ministry of Commerce communique allowing authorised export of locally processed ferrous and non-ferrous metals. No dealer register or domestic licensing text found. Weak.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No search spent on pawnbrokers or second-hand dealers; budget. The friperie search (under cat 5) returned only Algeria, Tunisia and Senegal content, no Togo rule.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No Togolese rule on gold buyers or jewellers found. Only the mining code (law 2003-012, 1996 code earlier) and a Mali comparison. Unverified whether a collector or comptoir licence exists.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Informal casse-auto trade spreading across Lomé (republicoftogo, 14 Apr 2026). No licence or register mentioned; dealers ask for proof of ownership to avoid receiving stolen goods; disputes with municipal technical services. Used-vehicle import duty depreciation rules from OTR, which are customs matters only. Weak.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: ECOWAS international transhumance certificate (1998 decision) and Togo's 2026-2030 transhumance plan under consultation (Mar 2026); FAO notes 60-day prior notice and multiple grazing taxes. No livestock market or trader card rules found. Weak.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Nothing usable. Food sanitary control sits with the Direction de l'Elevage; Public Health Code law 2009-007 and UEMOA Reg 007/2007 are listed but butcher licensing and health-card rules not found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Togo approved for honey exports to the EU in 2021 after a residue monitoring plan (2019-2020); about 2,000 beekeepers; cooperatives such as Adjengre. No domestic register duty found. Organic certification standard in draft (Feb 2026). Nothing new beyond K02-style export compliance, weak.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Vet law and vet pharmacy decree restrict sales to approved professionals; ministry approves practices and import/distribution establishments; April 2025 announcement of stronger controls on falsified vet drugs at markets and entry points; vet auxiliaries (PPV) cannot yet set up privately, law being updated. Small buyer pool.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water code law 2010-004 and implementing order put boreholes and wells above set thresholds under a declaration regime to the water minister; 2015 technical guide covers declaring existing boreholes and authorisation to abstract. Thresholds and a driller accreditation scheme not found. Weak.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: No Togolese emptier licensing found (Benin has one); ANASAP exists; Lomé waste pre-collection run by small associations and operators under municipal partnership. Evidence dated 2011-2019. Weak.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Togolese periodic inspection rule for lifts or pressure equipment found. Closest texts: order 0115 of 3 Feb 2020 on building classification (ERP, IGH) and decree 2017-30 on legal metrology bodies. Unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Rural and semi-urban mini water supply systems run mostly by user associations (AUSEPA), described as weak in technical and financial skills (2025); the ministry is moving to public-service delegation (pilot planned) and published a 2016 mini-AEP management guide. Possible niche: billing, tariff and reporting tool for AUSEPA or future small operators.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05. Plant protection directorate (DPV) approves importers and distributors by ministerial order; national pesticide committee (CPP) has registered 172 pesticides; informal trade in the southwest.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: No approval regime for private placement agencies found; Labour code 2006 presumably covers it. Unverified.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Search returned only French, Swiss and Belgian material; nothing on Togo found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: NGO decree 2022-002/PR (in force Apr 2023) requires notifying activities to prefects, mayors and regional planning directors on pain of suspension; circular of 7 Oct 2024 on recognition of foreign NGOs; a new association freedom law adopted by the cabinet in late 2025, parliamentary passage unconfirmed; online filing partial; many associations cannot get their recepisse. Halal supervision not searched.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi-moto trade regulated by a decree (number and date not found): agrement for each moto, driving licence, annual technical inspection, ownership proof, formal census; about 75,000 taxi-motos, many illegal. Minibus and trucking not searched.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Manual exchange agents need finance minister approval after BCEAO opinion under UEMOA Reg 09/2010/CM/UEMOA; monthly transaction report and register duties known from the Cote d'Ivoire guide (Togo equivalent unverified); new UEMOA external financial relations regulation in force Dec 2024. Market traders and street vendors not searched.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: about 400 operating but only 118 approved (SYNAPAEATO; article undated); 2019 suspension of category A registrations by the road transport directorate, current status unknown. No Togo text on nurseries. Tattoo studios, small food producers and hunting outfitters not searched.

coverage.found: Gaming-product tax (TPJH) expected up 50.8% in 2026 to CFA 4.4bn, driven by new games and more LONATO sales outlets. No licensing or reporting text found. Candidate C09b (weak).
